source.author: verg
source.text: Ut sese inclusit ruptisque immane catenis deiecit saxum, ferro quod et arte paterna pendebat, fultosque emuniit obice postis, ecce furens animis aderat Tirynthius omnemque accessum lustrans huc ora ferebat et illuc, dentibus infrendens.
source.text_original: Ut sese inclusit ruptisque immane catenis / deiecit saxum, ferro quod et arte paterna / pendebat, fultosque emuniit obice postis, / ecce furens animis aderat Tirynthius omnemque / accessum lustrans huc ora ferebat et illuc, / dentibus infrendens.
source.text_english: As soon as he had shut himself in and, with his chains broken, had hurled down the huge stone, which hung by iron and his father’s skill, and had strengthened the posts with a barricade, behold, the Tirynthian, raging in spirit, was at hand and, scanning every approach, kept turning his face now this way, now that, gnashing his teeth.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_original: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis / advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno / tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus / gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum / par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_english: Straightway the Tirynthian flies of his own accord to Argos of Inachus, where Hylas carries for him the poisoned darts and the bows that delight his eager shoulders—Arcadian weapons: he would indeed wish it, but his right hand is not yet equal to the burden, nor able to bear the club.
